To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

heat exposure is common, can cause health problems and reduce productivity in many jobs and that employers and workers consider heat to be a 'natural hazard', rather than an occupational health hazard, and so are not taking adequate precautions to avoid it.
Heat is a major health risk for workers in Australia and is associated with significant productivity losses.

(1) working in hot environments is common in many Australian industries, (2) heat exposure results in a range of adverse health effects and loss of productivity, and (3) employers and workers are not aware of the hazards of working in heat, or the actions that can be taken to prevent or minimize heat exposure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the health and safety of workers in the context of global warming and the associated increase in heat-related occupational health hazards.
the impact of heat on the health of workers, and the implications for health and productivity of working in Australia's summer heat.
the health and productivity implications of working in the heat in Australia, and with the need to develop and implement heat management strategies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

(i) heat exposure is a serious health risk in Australian workplaces, (ii) the burden of heat-related disease and lost productivity in the workforce is substantial, (iii) heat-related health effects and lost productivity are under-reported and under-appreciated, and (iv) the risk of heat-related health effects in the Australian workforce is likely to increase in future due to climate change.
the current heat exposure in Australia is not sustainable, and the situation needs to be improved.
the heat stress is a major problem for Australian workers and that the problem will be exacerbated by global warming.

the heat is a serious health and productivity issue in Australian workplaces.
heat exposure is an important and growing occupational health hazard in Australia.
